results.title: Integrate Binance Login with your web application
results.snippet:
Binance APIs utilize the [OAuth 2.0](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749) protocol for authentication and authorization. Binance supports common OAuth 2.0 scenarios such as those for web server, single page (browser based), mobile and native applications. This document will guide you through how your application communicates with Binance's OAuth 2.0 server to secure a user's consent for performing an API request on his behalf.
To begin, your application must identify the necessary permissions, or `scopes`. Visit the [Binance Developer Center](https://developers.binance.com/en/oauth-management), sign up for a Binance entity account, and from there, navigate to your console to create an OAuth application and get your own client ID and client secret. For now, Binance Login (Oauth2.0), is exclusively offered to close ecosystem partners. Please reach to our business team for further information.

results.snippet:
# OAuth 2.0 APIs for Binance APIs
```
Codecurl 'https://www.binanceapis.com/oauth-api/v1/user-info' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}'
```
**Parameters:**
| Name | Type | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| access_token | String | YES | |
**Response:**
```
Code{
"code": "000000",
"message": null,
"data": {
"userId": "e10e20b7f20947e7bd206b15ce3dae90"
},
"success": true
}
```
## API 2. Revoke access_token
```
Codecurl --request POST 'https://www.binanceapis.com/oauth-api/v1/revoke-token' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}'
```
**Parameters:**
| Name | Type | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| access_token | String | YES | |
**Response:**
```
Code{
"code": "000000",
"message": null,
"data": true, // true means clear access_token success
"success": true
}
```

- If you already have another pair for oauth login of Binance for your website, you can just use that one. So that you can share the openid between your website and web application.
1. Request for the `access_token` with the `clientId` and `secret` from Binance Server. It will return the `access_token` with expiration time.
2. Request for ticket with `access_token` from Binance Server. It will return the ticket with expiration time.
- Please make sure that your `secret` , `access_token` and `ticket` is saved on your server and cannot be accessed by others.
1. After the webapp is loaded on the Binance app, the developer should try to initialize the jssdk with the signature, which is calculated on the developer's server.
The fields to be signed include:
- clientId
- noncestr (nonce) (random string)
- Valid JS-SDK ticket
- timestamp(ts)
- url (URL of the current web page, excluding # and the part after it).

These methods are available in every CCXT language — TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, PHP, C#, Go and Java. results.title: Binance MCP Server
results.snippet:
# Binance MCP Server
Binance MCP Server
Connect your AI agent to Binance with a single URL. Your agent can read market data, check balances, trade Spot / Margin / Convert / USDⓈ-M / COIN-M Futures, and move funds between wallets inside a dedicated Agentic sub-account — no local install, no API keys on your device.

## What's an MCP?
Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI agents connect to external apps and services. Instead of just answering questions, an AI with MCP access can take actions on your behalf.
## What your agent can do
#### Check the market
"What’s the current BTCUSDT price and 24h change?" — tickers, order books, candlesticks, funding rates.
#### Check your balance
"Show my Agentic account balance across all wallets." — plus a read-only view of your main account.
#### Trade
"Buy $100 of BNB at market on spot." — Spot, Margin, Convert, USDⓈ-M Futures, and COIN-M Futures.
#### Move funds between wallets
"Move 2,000 USDT from my Spot wallet to my USDⓈ-M wallet." — inside your Agentic sub-account only.
## What your agent can access
When you connect, you choose which scopes to grant. Start with the least you need:
- **Market data** (public, no auth)

results.snippet:
Binance is excited to announce the launch of **Binance Agent OS**, a developer platform built as part of Binance Intelligence. It connects compatible AI applications and agents to supported Binance capabilities through user-controlled permissions.
Binance Agent OS brings together Binance APIs, Binance Wallet Agentic Hub, Binance x402, Binance Skill Hub, and support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), into a more coherent ecosystem for developers, users, and the broader industry.

Binance Agent OS is designed to reduce fragmentation across agentic crypto integrations. Instead of stitching together one-off connections, developers can access a controlled platform with a discoverable set of capabilities:
- **Binance APIs**: Programmatic access to supported Binance trading, market, wallet, and on-chain features.
- **Binance Wallet Agentic Hub**: Wallet capabilities designed for agent-driven interactions, subject to user permissions.
- **Binance x402**: Payment and settlement primitives designed to support agent-driven payment flows.
- **Binance Skill Hub**: A place for developers to discover and use modular capabilities across market data, wallets, trading, and on-chain activity.

results.title: Built for AI Agent Integration | Binance Blog
results.snippet:
Binance Agent OS is a gateway and toolkit for connecting AI agents to Binance. Our built-in MCP server currently supports trading and market data access, with payment and on-chain capabilities coming in future releases. In the meantime, developers can add these capabilities through other Agent OS tools.
## How to Connect Your AI Agent in Minutes
Connect your AI agent to Binance by adding the Binance MCP server to your agent environment, then authenticate it from your Binance account.
For Claude Code users:
1. **Add the MCP server.** Open your terminal, then copy and paste the following command:
*claude mcp add binance-mcp-server --transport http https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic*
2. **Open your agent environment** and enter /mcp. This lists your connected MCP servers, including binance-mcp-server.
3. **Start authentication.** Select binance-mcp-server and press Enter, then choose [Authenticate]. Your browser will redirect to an authentication page.
4. **Select your agent.** From the dropdown, choose which agent you want to connect to Binance.
